LanguageData.AM_Rec1: 'Any material' and 'Choose materials…' in the material menu of every build button.
LanguageData.AM_Rec2: A blueprint takes the material there is most of in storage; it keeps it while there is enough.
LanguageData.AM_Enabled_Desc: Master switch for the whole mod.
LanguageData.AM_Rule_Desc: Only materials there is enough of for the whole building. The material is chosen when the builder brings it – once it is delivered it does not change.
LanguageData.AM_GizmoAny_Desc: This blueprint is built from whatever material there is enough of (see the settings for which one). Off = only the material shown.
LanguageData.AM_GizmoChoose_Desc: Choose which materials the selected blueprints may use.
LanguageData.AM_Rec3: Buildings without a material choice (torch, campfire…) take another material of the same kind when the original is missing.
LanguageData.AM_FixedAuto_Desc: Buildings without a material choice (torch: 20 wood) may be built from another material of the same kind – any wood, any metal, any stone blocks, any cloth or leather. Components and other non-materials are never replaced. Can be turned off per blueprint.
LanguageData.AM_PreferOriginal_Desc: Use the original material while there is enough of it; a replacement only when it runs out. Off = the rule above decides.
LanguageData.AM_GizmoFixed_Desc: If there is not enough {0}, the builder brings another material of the same kind. Taking it down gives back what it was really built from.
LanguageData.AM_GizmoFixedChoose_Desc: Choose which materials the selected blueprints may use instead of the original.
LanguageData.AM_AutoAny_Desc: Every new blueprint of a building made from materials gets "any material" right away – handy when another mod (Better Architect…) shows its own material menu. You can still switch single blueprints back with their button.
LanguageData.AM_GizmoFrameStuff_Desc: Build the rest from another material (what was brought already goes back on the ground). "Any material": switches by itself when the current one runs out.
